headline: Iran deal hopes cool oil and yields, dollar slips; sterling leads, Taiwan dollar hits 18-month low
summary: The dollar index fell about 0.25% to near 101.75 after unconfirmed reports of a US–Iran compromise pulled oil off five-month highs and the 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 5.10%; a diplomat's denial trimmed the drop from a three-week low near 101.50. Sterling led on a strong UK jobs report, the loonie hit a four-week high and the won a two-year high, while the Taiwan dollar slid to its weakest since April 2025 and the peso held at a record low.
drivers: Iran headlines cut oil and yields

Reports of a Qatar–Pakistan brokered US–Iran compromise pushed WTI from above $100 toward $96 before a denial; the 10-year yield fell about 2–4bp to roughly 5.10% and the dollar index touched 101.50, its lowest since Oct 1. Fed hike odds for next week are down to about 15%, though a December hike is still largely priced.
BoE and BoC hawks lift GBP and CAD

UK unemployment fell to 4.7% against 4.9–5.0% forecasts and pay beat, so markets price about a 96% chance of a November BoE hike; sterling rose about 0.55% to near 1.3380 after 1.3409. The loonie hit 1.4033 as Alberta voted to stay in Canada and BoC hike odds held near 80%.

Foreigners sold Taiwan shares for a 10th day (about NT$80 billion) and the Kospi fell 3.7%, yet exporters' dollar sales lifted the won to 1,328.1 while the Taiwan dollar slid 0.172 to 32.617. A record 20-year JGB auction helped the yen.
view: Mildly weaker into the Fed (Oct 28): October hike odds are fading, oil carries a deal-headline risk premium and the index sits near the bottom of its 101.5–102.5 October range, but a 10-year yield above 5% and a priced December hike should stop a clean break below 101.5. Fade the dollar against the yen and the Canadian dollar, where central banks lean hawkish; keep backing it against the Aussie and, until Bank Indonesia acts decisively, the rupiah. A confirmed Iran deal would push the index toward 101; a Fed that locks in December would make me neutral.
ideas: Short from 158.50 is working: record JGB demand and a hawkish-leaning Ueda meet Tokyo's 159–160 guard; hold for 156.80, stop 159.60, about 2:1.
BoC hike odds near 80% and the 2-year gap narrowing; sell bounces into 1.4100–1.4130 for the 200-day near 1.3880, stop 1.4210.
MSCI's standalone threat still drives outflows; buy dips toward 17,950 for 18,250, but cut size before Bank Indonesia's Oct 21 decision.
review: No targets or stops hit: the USD/JPY short (filled 158.50) is about 0.3 in favour, EUR/USD's long from 1.1180 is about 0.5% up, the AUD/USD short filled near 0.7000 and is flat, and USD/TWD's 32.50–32.60 short is about 0.1 against but its 32.80 stop held; CAD, KRW and IDR entries were not reached, so CAD and KRW entries move lower.

eurusd.note: Up about 0.2% to near 1.1235 as French protests eased and the dollar slipped; capped near 1.1260.

view.call: Buy dips toward 1.1190; a priced December ECB hike gives support.

eurusd.why: Both sides helped a little. Overnight unrest in France calmed, so the euro steadied after Monday's slide, while Iran-deal reports pulled oil lower and trimmed the 10-year Treasury yield to about 5.10%, softening the dollar. Gains stalled near 1.1260 as French bond yields stayed elevated and strategists warned more euro weakness from France is still to be priced.
eurusd.outlook: I keep the long from dips toward 1.1190: the dollar's rate edge has stopped widening and the ECB is priced to hike. France caps rallies near 1.1270 until spreads narrow; a close under 1.1140 would end the call.
eurusd.watch: French spreads and budget talks, euro-area flash consumer confidence on Oct 22, the Fed on Oct 28 and the ECB on Oct 29.

gbpusd.note: Led the majors, up about 0.55% to near 1.3380 after a one-month high of 1.3409 on strong UK jobs data.

view.call: 1.3300–1.3450; buy dips, but the Oct 28 Budget caps it.

gbpusd.why: A UK story. Unemployment fell to 4.7% against forecasts of 4.9–5.0%, employment rose about 102,000 and regular pay growth picked up to 3.7%, so money markets moved to about a 96% chance of a BoE hike on Nov 5. Sterling hit its highest since Sept 18 against the dollar and about 83.8 pence per euro, its strongest since May 2025, helped by a softer dollar.
gbpusd.outlook: Bias is higher while the BoE is the only major central bank set to hike next month, but the Oct 28 Budget and gilt yields above 5.4% are a real risk, so I trade the 1.3300–1.3450 range from the bottom. A close above 1.3450 would turn me outright bullish.
gbpusd.watch: UK CPI on Oct 21, the Budget on Oct 28, the Fed on Oct 28 and the BoE on Nov 5.

audusd.note: Up about 0.3% to near 0.7000 on the softer dollar; the short entry zone has filled.

view.call: Sell 0.7000–0.7020; RBA is on hold while the Fed isn't.

audusd.why: The Aussie rose with other risk-linked currencies as the dollar slipped on lower oil and Treasury yields and the yuan touched its strongest since mid-2022. This was dollar weakness rather than an Australian story: there was no new local data, and the RBA's outlook still reflects last week's jump in unemployment to 4.7%.
audusd.outlook: I still sell this bounce into 0.7000–0.7020: the RBA has no reason to hike while the Fed keeps a December hike alive. A close above 0.7070 would end the call.
audusd.watch: Australia flash PMIs on Oct 23, China data and yuan fixings, and the RBA on Nov 3.

usdjpy.note: Down about 0.2% to near 158.2 after a record-demand 20-year JGB auction; the 158.50 short is in favour.
usdjpy.why: The yen did some of the moving. A 20-year JGB auction drew bids of 5.84 times the amount offered, the strongest since the bond was introduced in 1987, pulling the 20-year yield down about 5bp and easing fears about Japan's finances. Lower US long-end yields on the Iran headlines added to the dip, though the yen was the dollar's smallest loser among majors.
usdjpy.outlook: Asymmetric: Tokyo has made 159–160 the line, Ueda says underlying inflation is close to 2% and swaps price about an 80% chance of a December BoJ hike. I hold the short for 156.80; a close above 159.60 would mean Tokyo is tolerating more weakness.
usdjpy.watch: Japan trade data and September CPI on Oct 23, the Fed on Oct 28, the BoJ on Oct 30 and rate checks near 159.

usdchf.note: Down about 0.25% to near 0.8246 as the dollar eased; the 0.8300 sell zone was not reached.

view.call: Sell bounces toward 0.8290; the franc trend is intact.

usdchf.why: A dollar move. Lower oil and long-dated Treasury yields on the US–Iran reports weighed on the greenback across the board, and the franc tracked the euro, which steadied as French protests eased. There was no Swiss-specific news; markets still expect the SNB to hold at zero rather than cut below it.
usdchf.outlook: The franc trend is firm, so I'd sell bounces toward 0.8290 rather than chase at 0.8246. A close above 0.8360 would end the call.
usdchf.watch: European bond spreads, SNB comments on the franc and the Fed on Oct 28.

usdcad.note: Loonie hit a four-week high of 1.4033 after Alberta voted to stay; closed near 1.4055, down about 0.4%.

view.call: Sell bounces into 1.4100–1.4130; BoC hike odds near 80%.

usdcad.why: The Canadian side drove it. Alberta voted by a large margin to remain in Canada, removing a political risk, and swaps kept about an 80% chance of a 25bp BoC hike to 2.50% on Oct 28 after Macklem's warning on energy inflation. Canada's 2-year discount to the US narrowed to about 146bp from 160bp, and a softer US dollar did the rest.
usdcad.outlook: I lower the entry to 1.4100–1.4130 and target the 200-day average near 1.3880; a break of the 100-day near 1.4040 has opened that path. A close above 1.4210, the 10-day average, would end the call; a sharp oil drop on an Iran deal is the main risk.
usdcad.watch: Oil and Iran headlines, and the BoC and Fed decisions on Oct 28.

usdcnh.note: Yuan touched about 6.6775 offshore, strongest since July 2022; fix 6.72, strongest since Feb 2023.

view.call: Slow grind lower at the PBOC's pace.

usdcnh.why: The PBOC kept guiding the yuan higher, setting the midpoint near 6.72, its strongest since February 2023 but still about 390 pips weaker than estimates, so it is braking the pace. Loan prime rates were held for a 17th month after the 4.5% GDP beat, and the central bank will run daily overnight repos from Oct 21 as it studies an overnight policy rate. Exporter conversion and a softer dollar did the rest.
usdcnh.outlook: A steady, managed grind lower in USD/CNH; I keep 6.64 as the target and 6.71 as the stop above last week's highs. Fixes landing close to estimates would signal faster gains.
usdcnh.watch: Daily fixings versus estimates, the overnight repo rate set from Oct 21, and US–China trade headlines.

usdhkd.note: Pinned near 7.8485, just shy of the 7.85 weak-side limit.

view.call: 7.84–7.85, no trade; an HKMA defence would lift HIBOR fast.

usdhkd.why: USD/HKD stayed near 7.8485 because Hong Kong rates remain well below US rates, keeping the carry trade of selling HKD for USD attractive. Tuesday's slight fall in long-dated Treasury yields barely changed that gap, and the Hang Seng's roughly 1% drop added no fresh inflows.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade. A touch of 7.85 would force the HKMA to buy HKD and push HIBOR higher; until then it sits at the weak edge.
usdhkd.watch: HKMA intervention at 7.85, the aggregate balance and one-month HIBOR.

usdsgd.note: Eased about 0.2% to near 1.2775 with the broad dollar.

view.call: Mildly lower with the dollar; SGD is low-beta.

usdsgd.why: USD/SGD followed the broad dollar lower as oil and Treasury yields fell on the Iran reports, with a firmer yuan helping regional sentiment. The move was small because the MAS held its policy band on Oct 14 and the S$NEER is already near the strong edge, which limits how far the basket can rise.
usdsgd.outlook: Mildly lower if the dollar keeps easing into the Fed; I keep 1.272 as the target and 1.285 as the stop. SGD will lag other Asian currencies in any rally.
usdsgd.watch: Singapore CPI and the broad dollar into the Fed on Oct 28.

usdkrw.note: Won firmed 2.2 to 1,328.1 at the Seoul close, its strongest since Oct 2024, despite a 3.7% Kospi drop.

view.call: Sell rallies into 1,335–1,340; exporters keep selling.

usdkrw.why: Exporters, led by chipmakers, kept selling dollars, which outweighed foreign selling of about 535 billion won of Korean shares as the Kospi fell 3.7%. The won hit a fresh two-year high intraday at 1,325.4 for a third straight session, helped by the softer dollar index near 101.8 and a chip-driven current-account surplus.
usdkrw.outlook: The trend favours the won, so I lower the entry to 1,335–1,340 for 1,315. A heavy foreign equity exodus on weaker AI earnings is the risk; a close above 1,352 would end the call.
usdkrw.watch: Foreign flows in Seoul, Samsung and SK hynix, AI earnings this week and Korea's Q3 GDP.

usdtwd.note: Taiwan dollar fell 0.172 to 32.617, weakest close since April 2025, after touching 32.672.

view.call: Fade 32.50–32.65; the central bank is smoothing hard.

usdtwd.why: Foreign investors sold Taiwan shares for a 10th straight day, about NT$80 billion, taking the run to over NT$830 billion, and the Taiex fell 1.1% before Wednesday's futures settlement. Repatriation of sale proceeds and dividends overwhelmed central bank dollar sales, after it had dragged Monday's close back to 32.445 late in the day.
usdtwd.outlook: I keep fading the weakness: the central bank has said publicly it will act, foreign futures shorts are being trimmed, and settlement on Oct 21 may end forced selling. But outflows are winning for now; a close above 32.80 would stop the call.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign flows on the Taiex, futures settlement on Oct 21, TSMC and AI earnings, and central bank action.

usdmyr.note: Ringgit flat at 4.0805/4.0845 at the 6pm close as investors waited for the Fed.
usdmyr.why: The ringgit held still because the drivers cancelled out. Low odds of a Fed hike next week and a softer dollar index helped, but markets still expect a December Fed hike, and strong Malaysian data (third-quarter growth of 5.3% and 1.8% inflation) is already reflected in the price, so it stayed in a narrow range.
usdmyr.outlook: Range-bound around 4.07–4.10. Strong trade and low inflation support it, but it rarely moves far without the broad dollar.
usdmyr.watch: The Fed on Oct 28, oil prices and Bank Negara's Nov 5 meeting.

usdphp.note: Peso closed unchanged at its record low of 63.09; it traded 62.98–63.11 into Thursday's BSP.

view.call: 62.80–63.40 into Thursday's BSP; a skip would break 63.40.

usdphp.why: The peso held at its record-low close because high oil kept import dollar demand strong while the softer global dollar offered little relief. Traders also see the BSP smoothing moves above 63, and positions are light before Thursday's policy meeting. It is down about 6.8% this year.
usdphp.outlook: A 62.80–63.40 range into Thursday. Twenty of 22 economists expect a 25bp hike, with two calling for 50bp; a hike should steady it, while a skip would likely break 63.40.
usdphp.watch: The BSP decision on Oct 22, oil prices and BSP dollar sales near 63.20.

usdidr.note: Rupiah firmed slightly to about 18,010–18,030 as Jakarta curbed selling; JISDOR fixed at 18,006.

view.call: Buy dips toward 17,950; MSCI risk outweighs intervention.

usdidr.why: The rupiah steadied on local measures, not the dollar. The stock exchange halved the daily price-drop limit to 7% and moved to improve transparency after MSCI's standalone threat, so Jakarta stocks rebounded about 3%. Bank Indonesia said swaps and DNDF tools had drawn in $8–9 billion, and the JISDOR reference rate firmed to 18,006 from 18,050.
usdidr.outlook: I stay long the dollar on dips toward 17,950 while the MSCI threat stands, but Wednesday's decision is binary: Citi expects a 50bp hike, others 25bp or a hold. A large hike plus credible fixes for MSCI would end the call below 17,850.
usdidr.watch: Bank Indonesia's decision on Oct 21, the government's response to MSCI and bond auctions.

usdinr.note: Onshore market shut for Dussehra; offshore rate near 94.75 after Monday's 94.91 close.

view.call: 94.50–95.80; the RBI wants order, not a rally.

usdinr.why: Indian markets were closed for Dussehra, so the offshore rate drifted about 0.2% firmer with the softer global dollar and the dip in oil on Iran-deal reports. On Monday the rupee ended a six-day winning run at 94.91 as equity outflows and Brent near $108 lifted importer demand, after RBI curbs on spot dollar demand had driven a 2% gain the prior week.
usdinr.outlook: A managed 94.50–95.80 range. The RBI wants stability, not a rally, and oil is the swing factor; I wouldn't chase it either way.
usdinr.watch: Oil and Iran talks, RBI intervention near 95 and foreign portfolio flows.

eurjpy.note: Little changed near 177.7 as the euro and yen both firmed against the dollar.

view.call: 176–179; the BoJ on Oct 30 is the event risk.

eurjpy.why: Both legs gained on the dollar by similar amounts: the euro about 0.2% as French unrest eased, the yen about 0.2% after record demand at the 20-year JGB auction. With EUR/USD near 1.1235 and USD/JPY near 158.2, the cross ended near 177.7, almost unchanged.
eurjpy.outlook: Range 176–179. The ECB (Oct 29) and BoJ (Oct 30) meet back to back; a hawkish BoJ would break it lower, while a French budget deal would lift it.
eurjpy.watch: French bond spreads, Japan CPI on Oct 23, and the ECB and BoJ meetings.

cnhjpy.note: Near 23.70, close to the top of its range, as the yuan hit a four-year high.
cnhjpy.why: The yuan firmed to its strongest since mid-2022 on another strong PBOC fix, while the yen also gained after the JGB auction, so CNH/JPY held near 23.70, close to the top of its recent range.
cnhjpy.outlook: No edge in a 23.3–23.8 range: the PBOC slows yuan gains while Tokyo guards the yen's weak side. A break above 23.8 would need the yen to weaken through 159.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings and Japanese intervention signals.

watch: Next: UK CPI, Bank Indonesia and Taiwan futures settlement (Oct 21), the BSP (Oct 22), Japan CPI (Oct 23), the Fed, BoC and UK Budget (Oct 28), the ECB and BoJ (Oct 29–30), US–Iran talks and oil, and Tokyo's 159–160 line.
